proof_skeleton_nl: Fix integers m >= 2 and g >= 0. By the explicit Kunz-coordinate counting identity, the number N(m,g) of numerical semigroups with multiplicity m and genus g equals the cardinality of the Kunz slice K_{m,g}; the same identity with g replaced by g+1 gives N(m,g+1) = |K_{m,g+1}|. Next, establish finiteness of both K_{m,g} and K_{m,g+1}; this is needed before any cardinality comparison via injections. Then invoke the core combinatorial lemma asserting the existence of an injective map J_{m,g} : K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1}. The finite-set injection principle converts that injective map into the inequality |K_{m,g}| <= |K_{m,g+1}|. Finally, replace these cardinalities by N(m,g) and N(m,g+1) using the two counting identities. This yields exactly the desired monotonicity statement N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1).

steps.derives: For every integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, N(m,g) = |K_{m,g}|, where K_{m,g} is the explicitly defined set of positive tuples satisfying the multiplicity-m Kunz inequalities and having coordinate sum g.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the statement of L3.

steps.derives: For every integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, the set K_{m,g} is finite.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the statement of L4 applied with the given parameters m and g.

steps.derives: For every integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, the set K_{m,g+1} is finite.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L4 with the same integer m and with the genus parameter replaced by g+1. Since g >= 0, we have g+1 >= 0, so all hypotheses of L4 are satisfied. Therefore the set K_{m,g+1} is finite.

steps.derives: For every integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, there exists an injective function J_{m,g} : K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1}.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the statement of L5.

steps.derives: For every integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, |K_{m,g}| <= |K_{m,g+1}|.
steps.trivial_justification: From A2, the source set K_{m,g} is finite. From A3, the target set K_{m,g+1} is finite. From A4, there exists an injective function J_{m,g} from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}. Apply L6 to the finite sets A = K_{m,g}, B = K_{m,g+1}, and the injective map f = J_{m,g}. The conclusion of L6 is exactly |K_{m,g}| <= |K_{m,g+1}|.

steps.derives: For every integer m >= 2 and every integer g >= 0, the number N(m, g) of numerical semigroups with multiplicity m and genus g satisfies N(m, g) <= N(m, g + 1).
steps.trivial_justification: Apply A1 with genus parameter g to obtain N(m,g) = |K_{m,g}|. Apply A1 again with genus parameter g+1 to obtain N(m,g+1) = |K_{m,g+1}|. Step A5 gives |K_{m,g}| <= |K_{m,g+1}|. Substitute the two equalities into this inequality. The result is exactly N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1), which is the root theorem statement.
